The test image shows a soybean leaf with one prominent lesion: circular shape, light gray/white center, surrounded by a distinct dark purple-brown border ring. A few tiny dark spots scattered elsewhere on the leaf.

This pattern — circular lesion with gray center and dark reddish-brown margins — strongly suggests Frogeye leaf spot. Let me view one reference image to confirm.

The reference Frogeye leaf spot image shows circular lesions that have dropped out (shot-hole appearance), with reddish-brown borders — consistent with mature Frogeye lesions. The test image shows an earlier-stage lesion with the same circular shape and dark reddish-brown/purple border around a gray-white center, which is the classic Frogeye leaf spot presentation before the center falls out.

The match is strong: circular lesion, gray center, dark purple-brown border ring, on an otherwise healthy-looking leaf.

The reference images confirm this pattern, with mature lesions showing the same border before the center tissue drops out. No angular vein-limited lesions (bacterial blight), no pustules (bacterial pustule), and no powdery coating (powdery mildew)."}
